assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: unknown
driver_capability: limited

## Current capability

DeepSeek Harness has an in-process foreground `subagent` tool. Its native child uses a bare UUID and writes `origin: subagent` and `parentSession` in its durable header. The current adapter accepts that child form and links the child to its parent. The 3.1 and 3.2 live recordings verify this mechanism. The historical claim that the adapter rejected this form is obsolete.

## Missing end-to-end evidence

This cell has no valid orphan-cleanup recording. The preserved candidate `.build/failed-recordings/1980-dsh-3-4-orphan-2026-09-20-21-16-03/` contains no native child or `subagent` call. The local model used shell actions instead of the requested tool invocation. It therefore cannot prove or disprove child orphan cleanup after a shared-process exit.

## Driver limit

The interactive driver can send a prompt and terminate the DSH process. It has no primitive that directly invokes DSH's model-owned `subagent` tool. A valid recording must first observe a durable linked native child in working state, then observe the scoped cleanup after termination. Until that recording exists, daemon capability for orphan cleanup is unknown.
caveats: The 3.4 failed candidate is preserved outside replaydata at .build/failed-recordings/1980-dsh-3-4-orphan-2026-09-20-21-16-03/. It has no native child call, so it is not replay evidence.
The native child shares the parent DSH PID. A valid cleanup proof needs distinct linked child and parent sessions, then the shared-PID exit fanout. It must not require a distinct child PID.
The interactive driver cannot force a model-owned subagent call. A prompt-only run that uses shell actions instead is driver-limited evidence, not a daemon failure.
The historical bare-UUID and parentSession adapter defects were fixed and observed in the 3.1 and 3.2 native-child recordings.

sources.note: Official installed package reference: run_in_background:false waits for the child result in continuable mode.
Shipped standard preset mounts tool-subagent with provider spawn, toolName subagent, and continuable mode; the effective TUI dump confirmed these rows.
Official implementation creates the in-process child with a bare randomUUID and a distinct child Session.
childSessionMeta persists parentSession and origin:subagent in the child header.
Official persistence contract: each session has its own directory; committed records survive a crash; the backend does not delete session files.
Installed TUI source confirms that a subagent child id and persisted directory use the same bare id without a session- prefix.
Current adapter accepts validated bare-UUID native child directories.
Current source wires ParentSessionIDFromPath for durable native-child links.
Current adapter header reader validates native subagent origin and parentSession.
HandleWatcherExit fans a shared PID out to linked children before parents; HandleProcessExit and deleteWithChildren delete rows without a working transition.
Driver implements send, sleep, and sigkill and pins the local LM Studio model through per-run settings.
Live DSH recording: the pinned local-model turn stayed working for about 107 seconds and the process watcher emitted process_exited after the TUI ended.
Live DSH transcript: the qwen/qwen3.5-9b route reached its first bash tool call about 100 seconds after turn start, grounding the recipe delay and observation vector.

preconditions: dsh 0.1.5-rc.2 or newer is on PATH and the active TUI profile uses the standard preset
the active preset exposes the in-process subagent tool and accepts run_in_background:false; re-probe the live tool surface at record time
LM Studio is serving qwen/qwen3.5-9b through http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1; re-probe the live model roster at record time
irrlichd is recording with DeepSeek Harness transcript permission granted
setup: Create a fresh per-run cwd and launch the DSH TUI through the interactive driver
Apply the temporary LM Studio and qwen model patch, and set DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access, without modifying the installed TUI profile
Resolve the post-marker parent session.v3.jsonl.zstd before sending input

script.text: Use the subagent tool exactly once. Set description to orphan marker. Set prompt to: Run the bash command `sleep 240`, then reply with exactly CHILD_DONE and no other text. Set run_in_background to false so you wait for the child result. Do not take any other action. Do not reply until the child returns.

verify: the raw parent transcript contains exactly one subagent tool call whose arguments explicitly set run_in_background to false
events.jsonl shows a distinct child transcript_new and parent_linked before SIGKILL
the child reaches working before the kill and has no completed tool result or turn end
the shared-PID watcher emits process_exited for the child and parent after SIGKILL
no state_transition to working or waiting fires for the child after its process_exited cleanup edge
the recording reports agent deepseek-harness, model qwen/qwen3.5-9b, and non-zero tokens
recipe.scope_note: The 150-second pre-kill delay matches the slow local-model class represented by the opencode sibling and exceeds the measured approximately 100-second DSH delay to a first tool call. The 25-second post-kill settle matches the upper end of committed sibling recipes. The minimal one-child shape tests the same cleanup invariant as the canonical five-child case.
